newsitem.title: USA: Senate bill introduced to limit terms of US judges.
newsitem.headline: Senate bill introduced to limit terms of US judges.

text.p: A proposed constitutional amendment to set a 10-year term limit for federal judges, who now serve until they retire or die, was introduced in the Senate Wednesday by New Hampshire Republican Bob Smith.
Smith, a conservative, said term limits were needed to get rid of judges who abuse their power and who cannot be removed from office except for illegal conduct.
"Term limits for judges would establish a responsible and appropriate constitutional check on activist judges," Smith said at a news conference.

"Activist judges have taken control of prisons and school districts. They have ordered tax increases. Some have created new rules to protect criminal defendants that result in killers, rapists and other violent individuals being turned loose to continue preying on society," Smith added.

Judges who complete a 10-year term would be eligible for reappointment for a second term subject to Senate confirmation. The life terms of current judges would not be affected if the amendment became part of the Constitution.
A constitutional amendment must be passed by a two-thirds majority in both the Senate and House to be sent to the states for ratification.
